title: runtime-config-contract-and-sanity-checklist
author: Sofia Chen
body:
Summary:

This document defines the Runtime Configuration Contract for Redwood Inference services and provides a prescriptive sanity checklist and automated validation steps required for any config change that affects runtime behavior (startup, scheduling, GPU affinity, batching, KV cache heuristics, and tiered-fidelity routing). The goal is to reduce incident risk caused by misconfiguration, enable safe rollouts, and make operational ownership explicit.

Why this exists:

- Configuration drift is a frequent root cause of production regressions (mis-sized caches, inadvertent global toggles, invalid type changes).
- Runtime behavior is determined by a combination of service defaults, operator-managed overrides, and tenant-level hints; we need an explicit contract to keep changes safe.
- Developers, SRE, and platform engineers must share an unambiguous checklist and telemetry expectations for rollouts.

Scope:

- Applies to all services in the inference stack (edge proxies, request router, runtime shards, kv-coordinator, batching-service, prewarming-agent).
- Applies to changes to any config that: alters resource allocations, scheduling/placement, batching parameters, prewarm/warmup flows, model variant selection rules, telemetry sampling, or security-sensitive toggles (encryption/auth).
- Does NOT cover ephemeral per-request hints or customer-supplied prompt payloads.

Runtime Configuration Contract (high level):

1) Schema and Type Safety
- Every runtime config item must have a precise type, validation pattern, and a canonical default in code.
- Configs must be expressible in a JSON Schema or OpenAPI parameter declaration and validated pre-deploy.

2) Backward-compatible change rules
- Non-breaking additive changes (adding new optional keys) are allowed without broad coordination.
- Changes that modify default behavior, widen semantics, or change numeric floors/ceilings require an ADR or a staged rollout (see Rollout Strategy).

3) Ownership and Lifecyle
- Each config key must document an owner (team and primary contact), TTL for experimental flags, and a retirement policy.
- Experimental flags must include an expiration date in metadata and automated reminders.

4) Observability & Telemetry Guarantees
- Any config change that impacts runtime must declare at least three telemetry signals to be tracked (see Telemetry section) and a pre-change baseline window.

5) Safety Gates
- CI-level static validation + integration-level dynamic validation must pass before a rollout is permitted.
- Rollouts must provide an automated rollback path and explicit SLA thresholds that, if crossed, trigger immediate rollback.

Configuration Metadata Table (examples):

| key | type | default | validator | owner | experimental-ttl | safetynet |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| batching.max_batch_tokens | integer | 4096 | 1..65536 | runtime-team | none | must not increase >2x in canary |
| kv.cache.segment_count | integer | 256 | power-of-two, <=8192 | kv-team | 2026-09-30 | prewarm on change |
| prewarm.concurrent_jobs | integer | 4 | 0..128 | infra-ops | none | startup-time increase <10% |
| model.variant_order | array[string] | ["high-fidelity","low-cost"] | non-empty, known variants | model-onboard | none | commit must include compatibility tests |

Note: store the canonical JSON Schema in the repo: infra/config-schemas/runtime-config.schema.json and reference it in PRs.

Sanity Checklist (must be completed and recorded in CI for any PR that touches runtime-config):

A) Static validation (pre-merge)
- [ ] Schema validation (jsonschema) passes for all modified keys.
- [ ] Type and range checks included in unit tests.
- [ ] Owner metadata present (owner_team and contact alias).
- [ ] Experimental flags include expiration date.

B) Local integration tests (PR pipeline)
- [ ] Local runtime starts with the new config and reaches healthy state within baseline startup time + 20%.
- [ ] Migration/downgrade path exercised: start with new config, revert to old config, verify healthy.
- [ ] End-to-end synthetic inference against canary prompt set (report accuracy / fidelity metrics).

C) Canary rollout requirements (staged deploy)
- [ ] Canary traffic limited to <=2% per shard and <=5% of overall traffic for 24 hours.
- [ ] Observe telemetry for 1 rolling window (default 30m):
  - config.validation.failures (must be 0)
  - service.5xx_rate (no >0.5 percentage point increase over baseline)
  - latency.p50/p95/p99 (no >10% p95 regression)
  - startup.time (no >15% increase if change affects boot path)
  - model.quality.regression (no significant drift vs baseline prompts)
- [ ] Canary must be manually confirmed in the deployment dashboard before broader rollout.

D) Rollback triggers (automatic)
- Any of the following observed during the canary window should trigger automatic rollback:
  1) config.validation.failures > 0 (5 minute sustained)
  2) service.5xx_rate increase >= 1.0 percentage point sustained for 10 minutes
  3) latency.p95 degrade >= 20% sustained for 10 minutes
  4) model.quality.regression detected by automated evals beyond threshold

Rollout Strategy (recommended):

1) Prepare PR with config change, tests, and explicit owner metadata.
2) Merge to main after CI static/integration tests pass.
3) Deploy to shadow environment and run 3x longer synthetic workload (72h recommended for major changes).
4) Canary to 2% traffic for 24h, review telemetries and incident channels.
5) Expand to 10% for 12h, then 25% for 6h, then full rollout if stable.

Notes on Rollback: automated rollback must be time-bounded and non-blocking (i.e., do not require manual operator intervention unless the rollback itself fails). Log the rollback cause as an incident stub and create a post-change triage within 24 hours.

Telemetry and SLI checklist (minimum signals to attach to a config change):

- Business/service signals:
  - request.success_rate (per-route)
  - latency.p95 (per-route, per-model)
  - tokens.per_request and cost.per_request (important for batching changes)

- Platform/health signals:
  - service.startup.time
  - config.validation.failures
  - prewarm.job_failures and prewarm.queue_length
  - gpu.utilization and gpu.thermal_events (if change affects scheduling)

- Model-quality signals:
  - prompt_suite.accuracy and prompt_suite.bleu_or_f1 (depending on task)
  - embedding.cohort_consistency (for embedding pipeline changes)

Minimum acceptance thresholds (example):

- request.success_rate must remain within 0.5 percentage points of baseline over canary window.
- latency.p95 must not increase by more than 10% in aggregate; per-route exceptions must be documented.
- model-quality metrics must not regress by more than the pre-specified delta in the PR description.

Example config fragment (YAML) to include in PRs (must be validated against schema):

---
# example/runtime-config.yaml
batching:
  max_batch_tokens: 8192
  max_concurrent_batches: 8
kv_cache:
  segment_count: 512
  ttl_seconds: 86400
prewarm:
  concurrent_jobs: 8
  enable_warmup_probe: true

CLI validation tooling (examples):

# local schema check
infra/tools/config-validate --schema infra/config-schemas/runtime-config.schema.json example/runtime-config.yaml

# run integration start with config
DEV=1 infra/tools/run-local-runtime --config example/runtime-config.yaml --smoke-tests

Operational runbook snippet (post-rollout triage):

1) Identify whether failure is config-localized (grep logs for config-change-id and request-context).
2) If automated rollback executed, confirm rollback completed and observe telemetry for 30 minutes.
3) If rollback failed or not executed, escalate to runtime oncall and attach the PR link and change id.
4) Capture core diagnostics: heap profiles, kernel-scheduling traces, GPU utilization timeline, and prewarm logs.

Ownership and lifecycle obligations:

- Owners are expected to: maintain the JSON Schema, update owner metadata within 48 hours of team ownership changes, and respond to post-rollout triage requests within the SLO (4 hours for P1 issues, 24 hours for P2).
- Experimental flags must be automatically flagged for removal in 90 days; infra-tooling will generate periodic reminders.

Documentation and audit evidence requirements:

- Every config change deployed to production must have:
  - PR link, diff summary, and test artifacts attached to the deployment ticket.
  - Canary telemetry snapshot (baseline and canary period) uploaded to the release artifacts bucket.
  - A short post-rollout note in the change log: what changed, owner, and whether rollback occurred.

Open questions (to be discussed in runtime working group):

- What is the canonical policy for numeric range tightening vs. loosening for autoscaled values?
- How should we represent per-tenant overrides in the canonical schema while preserving global validation guarantees?

Appendix: Short ADR template for config-default changes

- Title: <short descriptive title>
- Problem statement: what user-visible or operational behavior changes?
- Proposed change: exact config keys and default values with rationale.
- Telemetry: baseline windows and metrics to observe.
- Rollout plan: staged percentages and durations.
- Rollback criteria: exact thresholds.
- Owner and reviewers: team + 2 reviewers.

References:

- infra/config-schemas/runtime-config.schema.json
- confluence/architecture-and-standards/infra-standards/service-config-convergence-and-gated-feature-flags-playbook-2024
